section_summary: This section documents escalating U.S. concern from 1934 through 1940 about alleged Japanese espionage, propaganda, commercial penetration, reconnaissance, and possible sabotage directed at the Panama Canal and its approaches. It includes War and State Department plans for systematic intelligence collection across Central America and northern South America, together with field reports from Costa Rica, Colombia, Honduras, El Salvador, Ecuador, Peru, and Japan. Many allegations—concerning fishing and mining concessions, paid agents, annotated maps, munitions shipments, and individual suspected spies—were explicitly unverified or treated skeptically by diplomatic officers.

subfiles.title: Continuation of report on anonymous threat notes and press handling
subfiles.about: Reports the handling and investigation of anonymous notes apparently warning of a threat to Canal Zone installations.
subfiles.summary: Gonzalez gave his copy to Consul General MacVitty, discouraged Ryan from publishing, and noted Admiral Crosley's precautions.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 548 forwarding a further communication from James Ryan
subfiles.from: Antonio C. Gonzalez, American Minister in Panama
subfiles.about: Forwards another communication from journalist James Ryan concerning the Canal Zone threat story.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 548 transmits a further letter from James Ryan.

subfiles.title: James Ryan's request for an official explanation of delayed reporting
subfiles.to: Governor of the Panama Canal; copy to the American Minister
subfiles.about: Requests letters explaining that Ryan delayed his news story at the Governor's request while competing services published the information.
subfiles.summary: Ryan complains AP and UP reported the alleged Gatun Locks plot while he kept silent; after release by Colonel Cruse he filed and asks the Governor to explain to his Hearst superiors.

subfiles.title: Embassy transmittal of Warrington Dawson's Special Report No. W.D. 1584
subfiles.from: American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Paris
subfiles.about: Forwards Warrington Dawson's report on the Japanese secret service.
subfiles.summary: Paris Embassy transmits Warrington Dawson's Special Report No. W.D. 1584 for departmental distribution.

subfiles.title: Special Report No. W.D. 1584: The Japanese Secret Service
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Paris; Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Translates and summarizes a French press article alleging worldwide Japanese intelligence activity and special surveillance of the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: Dawson reproduces an article from CYRANO describing Japanese intelligence networks from Vladivostok to Panama and claiming particular attention to American naval points. The article alleges that Japanese residents near Canal infrastructure created a sabotage risk and that Washington sought expanded surveillance rights from Panama. Dawson encloses the original French clipping.

subfiles.title: Le “Service secret” du Mikado
subfiles.about: French article alleging extensive Japanese intelligence operations and surveillance of strategic sites including the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: Le 'Service secret' du Mikado portrays Japanese professors, merchants, tourists and fishermen as a directed intelligence system, stressing Panama's water infrastructure and American demands for greater surveillance.

subfiles.summary: The notation records that the item was transferred to file 811F.812. The handwritten subject appears to read “Fleet.”

subfiles.title: Collection of information concerning Japanese activities in Central America and northern South America
subfiles.from: C. Burnett, War Department General Staff, G-2
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Latin American Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests State Department assistance in systematically collecting intelligence on Japanese activities that might threaten the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: War Department says Japanese espionage probably operates in Panama but its collection is inadequate; it proposes using diplomatic and consular posts to monitor twenty-one sensitive areas for suspicious activity.

subfiles.title: Japanese Espionage Activities in the Vicinity of the Panama Canal
subfiles.about: Summarizes the history, recent manifestations, and military implications of alleged Japanese espionage near the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: Résumé traces alleged Japanese intelligence direction from San Francisco and Mexico City to legations in Bogota and El Salvador, with naval interest in ports and oil, motorboat soundings and colonies, possibly supporting action against the Canal; meaning uncertain.

subfiles.title: Information Desired by War Department
subfiles.doc_type: strictly confidential circular instruction, mailing copy
subfiles.to: Certain American diplomatic and consular officers
subfiles.about: Directs overseas posts to assist the War Department by reporting foreign activities of possible military significance around the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: The circular requests reports on suspicious transient and resident foreigners, coastal reconnaissance, insincere commercial missions, improper official contacts, and negotiations for concessions. It also asks for information on commerce, immigration, propaganda, and politics, while emphasizing discretion and limiting attention to powers capable of threatening the Canal.

subfiles.title: List of posts receiving the War Department intelligence circular
subfiles.about: Lists the American diplomatic and consular posts selected to receive the intelligence-collection circular.
subfiles.summary: The distribution covers posts in Costa Rica, Colombia, Ecuador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, El Salvador, Venezuela, Curaçao, and Trinidad. It demonstrates the intended geographic breadth of reporting around the Caribbean and Pacific approaches to the Panama Canal.

subfiles.title: Information Desired by War Department
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Certain American diplomatic and consular officers
subfiles.about: Final copy of the circular requesting intelligence on foreign activities related to Panama Canal security.
subfiles.summary: The instruction repeats the War Department's requested categories of observation, including transient agents, residents, coastal soundings, commercial cover, diplomatic contacts, and concessions. Posts are told to exercise proper discretion and collect most information through their routine work.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1201: Information Desired by War Department
subfiles.from: Leo R. Sack, American Minister in Costa Rica
subfiles.about: Forwards the Costa Rican military attaché's response to the June 4 intelligence circular.
subfiles.summary: Sack transmits a memorandum prepared by Colonel Nicholas W. Campanole containing the information currently available in Costa Rica. He promises to report further information and notes that many relevant details had already been sent directly to the War Department.

subfiles.title: Memorandum responding to the War Department intelligence request
subfiles.about: Reviews available reports on foreign reconnaissance, fishing, colonization, shipping, and concessions at Puntarenas.
subfiles.summary: Campanole cites reports on Puntarenas reconnaissance and a foreign minister, foreign-manned tuna vessels, Reed's refrigeration project and a fishing colony; recommends not forwarding the memo to State.

subfiles.title: Negotiations for Mining Concession in the Vicinity of the Colombian Atlantic Coast
subfiles.from: American Consulate, Barranquilla, probably Raymond Phelan
subfiles.to: Department of State; American Legation, Bogotá
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese interest in Colombian oil land and an iron-ore concession near the Atlantic coast.
subfiles.summary: Consulate: Japanese Commercial Mission sought an oil concession near Tubara, with Japanese interest in a Tucurinca iron-ore mine promoted by questionable businessmen; informant Bachmann offered samples.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum on the Colombian mining concession
subfiles.about: Advises caution before attempting to interest American capital in the Colombian mine.
subfiles.summary: Memo: several concession holders have questionable reputations, so obtain a fuller Bogota investigation before acting on Bachmann's samples.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 187 requesting comment on the Barranquilla mining report
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Winthrop S. Greene, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Bogotá
subfiles.about: Requests the Bogotá Legation's assessment of the reported Colombian mining negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Instruction No. 187 asks Greene to comment by air mail on the August 18 Barranquilla mining report.

subfiles.title: Departmental reply to Raymond Phelan on the mining-concession report
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Raymond Phelan, American Vice Consul, Barranquilla
subfiles.about: Informs Phelan that no further departmental action is contemplated on his mining report.
subfiles.summary: Department says Phelan's report went to War and Navy, but given new Bogota information no further action is planned.

subfiles.title: Transfer sheet for files 894.20219/91A and /92
subfiles.about: Records the transfer of two related records to the protection file.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists file items 894.20219/91A and /92. Both were transferred to classification 811F.812 under “Protection.”

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 995: Japanese Activities in Colombia
subfiles.from: Winthrop S. Greene, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Provides a preliminary response to reports of Japanese interest in Colombian oil and mining concessions.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 995: confidential inquiries had not confirmed Japanese interest in the Tucurinca mine; the Colombian president said the government watches Japanese colonists, making an oil concession unlikely; Bachmann may have exaggerated.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Despatch No. 995: Japanese Activities in Colombia
subfiles.from: Winthrop S. Greene, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Greene's preliminary assessment of the Colombian concession reports.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats Greene's account of efforts to verify Japanese interest in Colombian oil and iron resources. It likewise records his skepticism about the mine report and his intention to seek more definite information.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1009: Japanese Interest in Iron Mine in the Department of Magdalena
subfiles.from: Winthrop S. Greene, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Reports findings from the Magdalena Fruit Company concerning the proposed iron mine and its promoters.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1009: company representatives doubted the claimed ore quality and promoters near Aracataca; Greene found no confirmation of Japanese involvement and notes earlier alarming reports often proved unfounded.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 216: Alleged Japanese Activities
subfiles.from: John D. Erwin, American Minister in Honduras
subfiles.about: Forwards Benjamin Guillén's allegations that the Japanese Legation recruited him to work in the Panama Canal Zone.
subfiles.summary: Erwin transmits Vice Consul Fred K. Salter's memorandum of a conversation with the visiting Salvadoran Benjamin Guillén. He emphasizes that the Legation could not verify Guillén's claims and that they might be partly or wholly false, but sends them because of War Department interest in Canal security.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Benjamin Guillén
subfiles.from: Fred K. Salter, Vice Consul and Third Secretary
subfiles.about: Records Guillén's allegations of Japanese bribery, influence efforts, and attempted recruitment for work in Panama.
subfiles.summary: Guillen claimed the Japanese Legation paid him $2,000 to suspend his anti-Japanese magazine and offered $10,000 to get Honduras's tariff on Japanese goods repealed; he fears Japanese monitoring of the American Legation in San Salvador.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 103: Alleged Activities of Benjamin Guillen
subfiles.from: Robert Frazer, American Minister in El Salvador
subfiles.about: Assesses Guillén's reputation and the plausibility of his allegations against the Japanese Legation.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 103: Guillen seems intelligent and fairly respected, his magazine reportedly Chinese-backed; Frazer finds his story plausible but questions entrusting large payments to a junior Japanese vice consul.

subfiles.title: Memorandum evaluating Japanese writing on Guillén's map and photographs
subfiles.about: Provides translations and an initial assessment of annotations on materials supplied by Guillén.
subfiles.summary: Memo: markings on Guillen's photographs mostly unintelligible but lighter writing reads 'Japanese Spy. Navy Department'; map captions mention future American bases; the reviewer doubts a genuine technical study.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 241: Alleged Japanese Activities
subfiles.from: John D. Erwin, American Minister in Honduras
subfiles.about: Forwards a map and photograph supplied by Guillén and records his expanded allegations about Japanese activity.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 241: Guillen says he took a photograph from Yoshida's baggage and an annotated map of El Salvador, names Shiraki's store as a map repository and Izawa as paying him $2,000, and cites failed Gulf of Fonseca fishing efforts.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Ecuadoran munitions shipments
subfiles.from: Sparks, Division of the American Republics
subfiles.about: Interprets reported arms shipments to Ecuador as legitimate Italian purchases rather than smuggling.
subfiles.summary: Memo: Ecuadoran munitions shipments should be substantial since Ecuador bought Italian munitions; secrecy is to hide quantities from Peru, not illicit import.

subfiles.title: Report of alleged war-munitions shipments to Ecuador
subfiles.from: John J. O'Keefe, American Vice Consul, Buenaventura
subfiles.about: Reports Max Hamilton's account of disguised Italian munitions cargoes passing through the Panama Canal to Ecuador.
subfiles.summary: Hamilton says the German ship Manizales carried forty-three tons of Italian munitions, with four similar shipments, declared as small dynamite; O'Keefe cannot confirm but sees no reason to doubt his motives.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Panama Despatch No. 459
subfiles.about: Redirects readers to a Panama despatch about a proposed cultural-economic mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Panama Despatch No. 459 (August 22, 1938): an invitation for Panama to send a cultural-economic mission to Japan.

subfiles.title: Peruvian Commercial Mission to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports the composition, sponsorship, itinerary, and stated objectives of a Peruvian commercial mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Peruvian commercial mission to Japan, invited and financed by Japanese organizations and led by Cesar de la Fuente; the stated purpose was trade and cultural understanding, but delegates called it a pleasure trip.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to letter concerning Japanese land purchases in Panama
subfiles.about: Redirects readers to a letter about the prospective use of roughly 5,000 acres purchased by Japanese interests in Panama.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a February 6, 1930 letter on Japanese land purchases in Panama, enclosing a letter to David Miles.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Nagasaki reporting Murakami in Colón
subfiles.about: Reports an allegation that Murakami was performing Japanese government espionage work in Colón.
subfiles.summary: Nagasaki telegram: an American informant says Murakami in Colon is in special Japanese government service, presumably espionage, posing as employee of a store acquired from Chinese merchants.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Nagasaki telegram concerning Murakami
subfiles.about: Paraphrases the allegation that Murakami was a Japanese government agent in Colón.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of the Nagasaki telegram identifying Murakami as presumed spy in Colon under cover of a former Chinese-owned store.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché report on an alleged threat to explode the Panama Canal
subfiles.from: U.S. Naval Attaché or naval intelligence source
subfiles.to: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.about: Reports that a Japanese officer recovering in a Callao hospital allegedly threatened to blow up the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: Naval attaché: a Japanese officer recovering from appendicitis at the British American Hospital was overheard saying he would explode the Panama Canal once fit to travel; shipping agents called him a chief engineer for west-coast ports.

subfiles.title: Duplicate telegram from Nagasaki reporting Murakami in Colón
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the telegram alleging that Murakami was conducting espionage in Colón.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate Nagasaki telegram on Murakami in Colon, posing as an employee of a store acquired from Chinese merchants.

subfiles.title: Duplicate paraphrase of Nagasaki telegram concerning Murakami
subfiles.about: Duplicate paraphrase of the Murakami espionage report.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate paraphrase naming Murakami a suspected Japanese agent in Colon with a store cover.

subfiles.title: Instruction transmitting the Murakami report to the Embassy in Panama
subfiles.about: Sends the Nagasaki telegram about Murakami to the Embassy for confidential information and filing.
subfiles.summary: Instruction sends the Embassy in Panama a paraphrase of Tower's February 6 telegram on Murakami; identical instruction to the Colon Consulate.

subfiles.title: Enclosure: paraphrase of telegram concerning Murakami
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; enclosed for the American Embassy in Panama
subfiles.about: Provides the Embassy with the paraphrased allegation that Murakami was a Japanese agent in Colón.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure: paraphrase saying Murakami was allegedly engaged in espionage, ostensibly employed at a store taken over from Chinese merchants.

subfiles.title: Instruction transmitting the Murakami report to the Consulate at Colón
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Colón
subfiles.about: Sends the Nagasaki telegram about Murakami to the Colón Consulate for confidential information and filing.
subfiles.summary: Instruction sends the Colon Consulate a paraphrase of the February 6 Nagasaki report on Murakami; the Embassy in Panama receives a similar one.

subfiles.title: Enclosure: paraphrase of the Murakami telegram for Colón
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; enclosed for the American Consulate at Colón
subfiles.about: Provides the Colón Consulate with the allegation that Murakami was conducting Japanese espionage under commercial cover.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure for Colon: an American informant identifies Murakami as serving the Japanese government in Colon, working for a former Chinese-owned store.
